title: Practice Quiz: Execution Order & Program Flow

questions.question: In what order does the Python interpreter execute statements in a program?

options.text: Sequentially from top to bottom, one line at a time.
Randomly based on which line is the shortest.
From bottom to top in reverse order.
All lines simultaneously at the exact same millisecond.

questions.explanation_correct:
✅ EXCELLENT!
Python executes instructions strictly top-to-bottom, line-by-line in sequential order.
questions.explanation_incorrect:
❌ Not quite!
Python is sequential: it begins at line 1, finishes it, then proceeds to line 2, and so on.

questions.question: What will be printed in the console when this script runs?

options.text: Morning Afternoon Evening (all on one line)

questions.explanation_correct:
🎯 SPOT ON!
Each print() statement outputs on a new line in the exact order written from top to bottom.
questions.explanation_incorrect:
❌ Try Again!
Each print() executes in top-to-bottom order and places its text on a new line in the output terminal.

questions.question: If Line 2 contains a syntax error in a 3-line script, what happens?
questions.code:
print("Line 1")
print("Line 2"   # Missing closing parenthesis
print("Line 3")

options.text: Python halts and reports the error; Line 3 never runs.
Python ignores the error on Line 2 and continues running Line 3.
Line 3 runs first, followed by Line 1.

questions.explanation_correct:
💡 NICE!
When Python hits an error during execution or parsing, it immediately stops. Later lines are not executed.
questions.explanation_incorrect:
❌ Not quite!
Python stops execution immediately upon encountering an unhandled error. Subsequent lines do not run.

questions.question: What will be the console output of this code?
questions.explanation_correct:
🔍 WELL DONE!
Line 1 prints 10, then Line 2 prints 20 on the next line. They are not added together because they are separate print commands.
questions.explanation_incorrect:
❌ Try Again!
Because these are two separate print() statements, 10 is printed first, followed by 20 on a new line.

questions.question: True or False: Does Python decide the order of lines based on which variable seems most important?

options.text: False — Python strictly follows the written top-to-bottom order regardless of meaning.
True — Python rearranges variables to the top automatically before running anything.

questions.explanation_correct:
🏆 MODULE COMPLETE!
Computers have no common sense or concept of 'importance'—they execute strictly in the sequential order you write!
questions.explanation_incorrect:
❌ Almost!
Python never rearranges your code based on 'importance'. It executes lines strictly in the order you wrote them.
